Affinity
uh-FIN-ih-tee
noun
From Latin affinitas, relationship by marriage; in Kings and Chronicles, royal marriage alliance, often spiritually dangerous.

📖 Biblical Definition

Affinity in the historical books is kinship by marriage, especially the political marriages of kings. Solomon made affinity with Pharaoh king of Egypt and took Pharaoh’s daughter. Jehoshaphat, rich and honorable, joined affinity with Ahab. The word is not neutral sociology. Scripture records these affinities as hinge points of compromise. Solomon’s Egyptian marriage sat near the beginning of a heart turned by many strange wives. Jehoshaphat’s affinity with Ahab pulled a good king into a bad war and a near ruin of the Davidic line. Affinity teaches that marriage is never a private preference only; it joins houses, worships, and futures. The unequal yoke is not a modern invention of preachers. It is written in the fall of wise Solomon and the folly of godly Jehoshaphat. The church must recover a holy suspicion of affinities formed for status, trade, or romance without the fear of the LORD. What you join in marriage, you join in covenant consequence, and the prophets will ask whether you should help the ungodly and love them that hate the LORD. Kings fell by that door; common households still do when they join light with darkness and call the mixture love.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Relationship by marriage; in Scripture, royal marriage alliances that often opened doors to idolatry and shared ruin.

expand to see more

AFFINITY, relation by marriage; alliance through a spouse.

Solomon made affinity with Pharaoh by marriage.

Jehoshaphat joined affinity with Ahab.

Such bonds join worship and policy, not only households.

Unequal affinity is a historic snare for the people of God.

📖 Key Scripture

1Ki 3:1 — "And Solomon made affinity with Pharaoh king of Egypt, and took Pharaoh's daughter, and brought her into the city of David, until he had made an end of building his own house, and the house of the LORD, and the wall of Jerusalem round about."

2Ch 18:1 — "Now Jehoshaphat had riches and honour in abundance, and joined affinity with Ahab."

1Ki 11:1 — "But king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, and Hittites;"

2Ch 19:2 — "And Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him, and said to king Jehoshaphat, Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate the LORD? therefore is wrath upon thee from before the LORD."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Modern romance ideology treats affinity as pure chemistry; Scripture treats marriage alliance as moral and spiritual bond with public consequence.

expand to see more

The corruption is the doctrine that love legitimates every bond. Solomon’s affinity looked like wise diplomacy; it became a corridor for idols. Jehoshaphat’s affinity looked like peace among cousins; a prophet asked, Shouldest thou help the ungodly? Another corruption is reducing marriage to contract without worship. Biblical affinity always risks shared altars. The church must teach courtship and marriage under the fear of God, not under the myth of autonomous affection.

Soft culture also treats warnings about unequal yokes as bigotry. The text is kinder and harder: it shows the wreckage in kings so that common saints may fear before they join houses.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Affinity is marriage-bond alliance; in Kings it often names the snare by which kings joined themselves to idolatrous houses.

expand to see more

Latin — affinitas, marriage relationship.

Solomon — affinity with Pharaoh by Pharaoh’s daughter.

Jehoshaphat — affinity with Ahab.

Danger — shared policy and shared idolatry.

Law of love — marry in the Lord, not by status alone.

Usage

"Solomon made affinity with Pharaoh king of Egypt."

"Jehoshaphat joined affinity with Ahab to his hurt."

"Affinity joins more than two persons; it joins ways of worship."
